newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Post-op Yeltsin moves to rest home to convalesce.
newsitem.headline: Post-op Yeltsin moves to rest home to convalesce.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin moved from hospital to a government rest home on Friday to continue his convalescence from open heart surgery, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Reporters at the scene said they saw Yeltsin's motorcade leave the Central Clinical Hospital about 9.15 am (0615 GMT) heading towards the nearby Barvikha sanitorium.
NTV commercial television later showed Yeltsin, wearing a fur hat and long dark coat, waving cheerfully as he stepped into the presidential Mercedes-Benz limousine.
Yeltsin, 65, is said to be making steady progress after his November 5 quintuple bypass operation but doctors have warned him against taking things too fast.

On Wednesday, in his first public appearance since before his operation, Yeltsin said that he was in fighting mood and would return to work after a spell in Barvikha. He was shown walking slowly and stiffly, but he spoke in a firm voice and there was colour in his cheeks.

The presidential press service said Yeltsin would probably spend two or three weeks at Barvikha, a complex including a sanatorium and government residences near Moscow. Aides say Yeltsin will return to the Kremlin by the end of the year.
